toml:
# Lunar reference-station coverage with terrain: the bundled lunar-station-coverage scenario
# with a per-site horizon ray-marched over a real lunar digital elevation model at the
# station and at every user point, in place of the flat elevation mask alone.
#
# Terrain: [terrain] below. Each site's horizon is ray-marched (src/lunar_terrain.rs) over
# the vendored LRO LOLA south-polar DEM crop, data/lunar-dem/ (public domain; NOTICE.md
# there gives the source URL, SHA-256, crop and resample steps), at 1200 m per pixel, with
# the Moon's radius and curvature, from a 2 m mast, every 1 deg of azimuth out to 150 km. A
# satellite counts at a site when it clears both the flat mask_deg and the horizon at its
# azimuth. A stated profile can be added with station_horizon or user_horizon (rows
# [azimuth_deg, elevation_deg], labelled with a source); with both, the cut is their maximum.
#
# HONESTY: MODELLED. Under the stated assumptions below the model gives these figures. Not
# a statement about the performance of any real system; no TRL or heritage claim. The
# horizon is line of sight over a 1.2 km grid: relief below a pixel is smoothed away, a ray
# leaving the crop ends there, and there is no diffraction or terrain multipath. Site
# positions used for ranging stay on the mean lunar sphere; the DEM sets the horizon only.
# The station site (89 S, 0 E) and the constellation are ILLUSTRATIVE, as in
# lunar-station-coverage.toml; the terrain is the measured DEM, resampled.
#
# This scenario reads the DEM from the repository (data/lunar-dem/), so it is not bundled
# in the binary: run `kshana scenarios/lunar-station-coverage-terrain.toml` from a checkout.
kind = "lunar-station-coverage"

# Constellation. ILLUSTRATIVE: the in-tree LCNS-class Keplerian set (an elliptical orbit
# favouring the south pole), the same as lunar-differential-pnt's.
n_sats = 8             # ILLUSTRATIVE
sma_km = 9737.4        # ILLUSTRATIVE (about 8000 km above the mean lunar radius)
eccentricity = 0.6     # ILLUSTRATIVE
inc_deg = 57.7         # ILLUSTRATIVE
argp_deg = 90.0        # ILLUSTRATIVE (apolune over the southern hemisphere)
mask_deg = 5.0         # ILLUSTRATIVE (the moonlight-service-volume default)

# Station: a known site near the south pole.
station_lat_deg = -89.0    # ILLUSTRATIVE (a south-polar site; not a published location)
station_lon_deg = 0.0      # ILLUSTRATIVE
station_height_m = 0.0     # ILLUSTRATIVE (on the mean lunar sphere)
survey_sigma_m = 0.30      # ILLUSTRATIVE (the in-tree lunar frame-realisation allocation, itself MODELLED)

# Error model: common-mode orbit and clock errors, as in lunar-differential-pnt. The
# line-of-sight SISE this gives is sqrt(orbit_err_m^2 / 3 + clock_err_m^2) = 65 m.
orbit_err_m = 100.0        # ILLUSTRATIVE
clock_err_m = 30.0         # ILLUSTRATIVE
noise_m = 0.0              # ILLUSTRATIVE (no receiver noise)
latency_s = 10.0           # ILLUSTRATIVE (no published correction latency)
quantization_bits = 8      # ILLUSTRATIVE (no published correction message)

# User grid and time.
grid_lat_max_deg = -80.0   # the region: 80 deg S to the pole
grid_lat_step_deg = 2.0    # rings every 2 degrees (coarser than the flat scenario, to keep the DEM ray march light), plus the pole
t_start_s = 0.0
t_span_s = 86400.0         # one day
t_step_s = 600.0           # every 10 min
n_trials = 100             # Monte Carlo trials per epoch (fewer than the flat scenario, for run time)

# Thresholds, stated before the run and never fitted.
accuracy_threshold_m = 1.0 # coverage: the percentile 3-D error at most this
percentile = 95.0
alert_limit_m = 10.0       # ILLUSTRATIVE: no public alert limit exists
residual_sigma_m = 5.0     # ILLUSTRATIVE (lunar-differential-pnt's default)
p_hmi = 1e-4
seed = 42

# Terrain horizon masks (src/lunar_terrain.rs). Source: LRO LOLA LDEM_75S_240M (PDS data set
# LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0), cropped and 5 x 5 block-mean resampled to 1200 m; data/lunar-dem/NOTICE.md.
[terrain]
dem_path = "data/lunar-dem/lola_ldem_75s_1200m_crop.toml"
antenna_height_m = 2.0     # ILLUSTRATIVE (a mast on a lander deck)
azimuth_step_deg = 1.0
max_range_km = 150.0       # ILLUSTRATIVE (rays end here or at the crop edge, about 420 km from the pole)
